androidDeckTracker.onboarding.closeAppNo: This stops tracking and removes the notice. Forcing the app closed from the phone cannot send its own notice.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.intro: Please read the instructions below to set up Firestone on your phone. It's a one-time setup, and we'll guide you through it to make it as easy as possible.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.overlayPer: The deck list is display-only, so it does not take taps meant for Hearthstone. A small button shows or hides it.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.pairNotRea: The code screen closed before the code was sent. Show the code again, leave that screen open, and tap Enter code on the Firestone notification.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.pairReady: Tap Enter code. Type the 6 digits in the box that opens on this notification. Do not return to Firestone until the code is sent.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.pairWaitin: A button will appear on this notification. Tap it to open a text box. Leave the pairing screen open.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.pairWrongC: That code did not work. Type the code shown on screen.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.readyBody: Start a Hearthstone game. The deck list appears over the match.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.reportFail: The report could not be sent. Try again when you are online.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.setupBody: Tap Continue when you are ready for the next screen.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.shizukuIns: Shizuku lets Firestone read Hearthstone's log files.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.shizukuSta: Open wireless debugging, start Shizuku, then come back. You need to do this again after every reboot.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.shizukuSto: Shizuku stopped, usually after a reboot. Tap Set up to open it. On a trusted Wi-Fi it can start itself next time.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.signedIn: Signed in as {name}. Finished games are saved to this account.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.signedInNo: Your games are now synchronized to your account, and can be retrieved from the desktop application.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.signInBody: Tap to sign in with Battle.net, which will let you save all your games to your Firestone account. Your Battle.net info is never shared with Firestone.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepAllowI: Tap Continue. Android opens a setting for Firestone. Turn on Allow from this source, then come back here.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepDevelo: Tap Continue. If developer options are already on, that screen opens. If they are not, the phone info screen opens. Scroll to Build number and tap it 7 times, until the phone says developer options are on, then come back.
Developer options are still off. Tap Continue, then tap Build number 7 times on the phone info screen.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepGrant: Tap Continue. Android will ask whether Firestone can use the helper. Tap Allow.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepInstal: Tap Continue. Android will ask you to install the helper Firestone needs. Confirm the install, then come back to this screen.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepNearby: Tap Continue. Android will ask to let Firestone find wireless debugging on this phone. Tap Allow.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepOverla: Tap Continue to let Firestone show on top of the game. Find Firestone in the list that will appear, and allow it to display over other apps. Then come back here.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepPair: The 6-digit code is typed in the Firestone notification, not on this screen and not in Settings. Tap Show the code. In Settings, tap Wireless debugging, then Pair device with pairing code. Leave that screen open. On the Firestone notification, tap Enter code and type the 6 digits in the box that opens.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepStart: Tap Continue to start the helper. Stay on this screen. It takes a few seconds. If a pairing code is needed, the next step explains it.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepUnsupp: This Android version cannot run the tracker.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepWifi: Tap Continue. Join a Wi-Fi network, then come back. Wireless debugging cannot be turned on without one.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepWirele: Tap Continue. Find Wireless debugging and turn the switch on. If the phone asks about this Wi-Fi, allow it. Then come back.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.title: Set up the deck tracker
androidDeckTracker.overlay.notificationT: Your Hearthstone games are being recorded
androidDeckTracker.overlay.restartText: Firestone put back a setting Hearthstone only reads at startup. Quit Hearthstone completely and open it again so games keep being recorded.

website.uninstall.comment.body: A few words is enough. Leave a contact if you want a reply.
website.uninstall.comment.title: What should we know?
website.uninstall.competitor.title: Which app are you switching to?
website.uninstall.faq.body: If nothing appears at all, it's usually only a matter of enabling the Hearthstone overlay in Overwolf's settings. Please see the FAQ below.
website.uninstall.faq.title: Some simple steps are usually enough to fix it
website.uninstall.page-subtitle: If you don't mind, we would love to know why you're uninstalling - it just takes a few seconds.
website.uninstall.page-title: We're sorry to see you go
website.uninstall.premium.body: A Premium subscription turns the ads off and unlocks the extra overlays and stats.
website.uninstall.premium.title: Premium removes the ads
website.uninstall.reasons.overwolf: I liked the app, I just don't want to use Overwolf
website.uninstall.reasons.reinstall: I had an issue, and am uninstalling to try to fix it
website.uninstall.standalone.body: There is a build that does not need Overwolf. While it's still in closed beta, it's the same Firestone: deck tracker, overlays, and the rest. Would you like to try it?
website.uninstall.standalone.title: Firestone without Overwolf
website.uninstall.thanks.body: We wish you all the best, and will welcome you back anytime. If you left a contact, we'll get back to you as soon as possible.
website.uninstall.thanks.title: Thanks for telling us
